Diabetes is a worldwide problem that affects 12% of people in the USA. One solution that our industry sponsor, MiniMed, developed to help people manage diabetes is through using Continuous Glucose Monitors to track blood sugar and link it to an automatic insulin delivery pump. However, they don’t have the production power to manufacture these devices at a rate that keeps up with consumer demand. They came up with several solution ideas to improve manufacturing cycle time for the blood sugar sensor component, but never made it past ideation as it was difficult to test and implement them due to stringent ISO 7 medical device cleanroom standards, harsh corrosive solutions that all equipment is exposed to during the manufacturing process, and limitations with other moving parts of the sensor manufacturing pipeline. My team of 7 is developing a new sensor clamping fixture that will reduce the manufacturing cycle time, production cost, and ergonomic strain on operators using the equipment.

So far, my tasks have included:
- Project scoping and client interviewing
- Prototyping
  - Prototyped several new clamping designs, including a pen-click lock mechanism and a sliding bar lock mechanism
  - Produced low-resolution prototypes with readily available springs and screws
  - Produced higher-resolution prototypes through SolidWorks parts and assemblies, and 3D printing
- Materials analysis
  - Researched suitable materials to comply with ISO 7 cleanroom standards and highly corrosive electroplating baths
